subject: Interop stress test + retention offer
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Brooks <anna.brooks@helixretail.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Interop stress test + retention planning

Hi Anna —

Quick follow-up from our call last week. I heard Helix has an incoming bake-off and that the competitor has flagged throughput issues at longer sequence lengths. We'd like to offer a focused interoperability stress test to validate performance and fidelity at Helix-scale and produce an objective benchmark you can share internally.

What we propose:
- 48-hour dedicated test window against a mirrored workload (we provide scripts)
- Throughput/latency breakdowns by sequence length and concurrency
- Token-cost projection for your peak/steady-state scenarios
- A short commercial retention offer tied to capacity guarantees if we meet the targets (draft attached)

If this sounds useful, I can get Karthik and Naomi to scope the technical plan and Marissa to finalize the commercial terms. Timeline: we can spin up a test cluster as soon as next Wednesday.

Attaching an outline of the approach.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(d) 415-555-0102

Attachments: interop_stress_test_plan.pdf
From: Anna Brooks <anna.brooks@helixretail.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@helixretail.com>, procurement@helixretail.com
Date: 2028-06-20T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interop stress test + retention planning

Thanks Dylan.

We are indeed running an internal evaluation and the engineering team has seen some divergences in behavior under load (longer chats + multi-agent flows). Before we commit to any timeline-sensitive decisions, we need a reproducible test that mirrors our traffic patterns, including:
- 3x normal concurrency spikes
- sequences out to 8k tokens with KV cache behavior
- sample multi-request flows for tool-calling latency

Can your test plan include a list of exact scenarios and the scripts you’ll use? Also procurement asked for any commercial commitments to be in writing (DocuSign preferred). I’ve looped Samir and procurement.

Anna
Anna Brooks
Head of Platform Engineering, HelixRetail
anna.brooks@helixretail.com

Attachment: bakeoff_requirements.docx
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Interop stress test + retention planning

Marissa / Karthik / Naomi —
Forwarding Anna’s note. Helix is asking for a reproducible stress test (8k tokens, multi-agent flows, concurrency spikes) and wants commercial terms documented for procurement. Can we commit to:
1) Karthik: a 48-hour dedicated test with scripts and a small dedicated cluster; provide the plan and exact infra needs by EOD Monday.
2) Naomi: CS will run an onboarding checklist and a runbook for the test window — who’s on call for the 48-hour window?
3) Marissa: commercial retention offer (time-limited credit + price protection for 8 weeks) — draft a DocuSign-friendly offer we can send to procurement.

Target: send Helix the full package (test plan + doc for procurement) by Tuesday COB so they can approve the window.

Thanks,
Dylan

Subject: Re: Interop stress test + retention planning — technical plan

Hi Anna / Samir —

Thanks for the details. Attached is a runnable plan (interop_stress_test_plan.pdf) that includes:
- Exact request/response scripts (we’ll share a repo)
- Data profile and synthetic trace generator configured to match the bakeoff_requirements you sent
- KV/cache warmup procedure and sequence-length buckets (2k / 4k / 6k / 8k)
- Concurrency profiles including 3x spike pattern and a soak phase
- Metrics we’ll collect: p95/p99 latency per token, tokens/sec, memory/KV hits, and model output divergence via sample prompts

Operational asks from Helix:
- Short-lived API key with test-only access (rotate after window)
- Representative sample payloads (anonymized) for the multi-agent flows

We can provision a 4-GPU temporary test cluster and run the 48-hour window on your preferred dates. Expect an initial results packet within 24 hours after the window closes.

I’ll be available during the run and can provide real-time traces into a shared dashboard.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: interop_stress_test_plan.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2028-06-23T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Commercial: limited retention offer for HelixRetail

Hi Anna / procurement team —

Thanks for the clarity on the bake-off requirements. We appreciate the chance to demonstrate fidelity at scale. Per Dylan’s note, attached is a short-form retention offer:
- 8-week price protection from day of signature
- $50k in trial credits applied to the bake-off cluster (applied if Redwood meets the agreed throughput/latency thresholds)
- Priority onboarding, plus one dedicated week of optimization with our Performance Engineering team

If that aligns, I can populate a DocuSign and route to your procurement contact. To be transparent, this offer is contingent on completion of the controlled test and mutually agreed success criteria.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turnaround from you all.

Positive next steps from Helix:
1) We’ll provide the sample payloads and a test API key (security will scope it as test-only).
2) Procurement is okay to accept a DocuSign for the retention_offer_v1.pdf once Marissa populates it with standard PO/incorporation language.
3) Can we run the 48-hour window June 29–30? Engineering would like live access to the dashboard.

Samir — can you confirm your team’s availability for the 29–30 window?

Anna
